title: Milling Gantry
pages: Craft the controller with a Spindle Gearbox at the centre, three pistons in the top corners and bottom-right, with a Belt-Pulley Drive in the bottom-left, a Power Contactor on top, a Linear Guide either side of the gearbox and a Cemented Carbide Insert at the bottom centre. Craft the contactor from three Sealed Steel Plates and one Stamped Contactor Enclosure around a Copper Busbar on top, two Wound Coils, redstone and a Limit Switch; the coil closes the spindle power path while the switch supplies its control signal. The busbar is the rigid main conductor that the contacts bolt onto: hot-press Annealed Copper into Tempered Copper Sheet in the Copper Hot Press (100 ticks, 8 FE/t), then hold two sheets and right-click the formed Broach Press to punch one slotted Copper Busbar. A loose copper ingot, an unpunched sheet or Annealed Copper cannot replace it. Current rating, skin effect and busbar heating are abstracted. A bare redstone block cannot replace it in the controller craft. Two Carbide Powder Blends and an iron nugget make a Carbide Insert Blank; sinter it in the Copper Hot Press for 240 ticks at 16 FE/t. This flat, four-edge WC-Co cutter handles abrasive milling; the round drawing nib cannot replace it. Put a redstone block directly beneath the controller as the multiblock anchor and an anvil directly above it. Face four ordinary pistons inward against its horizontal sides.

The belt drive links an offset motor to the spindle. Make two Flanged Rings from separate four-iron batches in the tier-4 Flange Press, then loop two leather strips around them with a string cord in the centre. Install the assembled Belt-Pulley Drive at the controller craft bottom-left; a fourth piston or loose ring cannot replace it. The iron sheaves and corded leather represent a friction belt: distance between shafts is useful here, while tension, slip and pulley ratio are abstracted. The DOE motor-drive sourcebook describes offset positioning and speed changes by sheave diameter. Feed iron batches into the Flange Press and extract rings for repeated drive assembly.

The gantry head travels on two Linear Guides (profile rails): a carriage block rides a hardened rail on recirculating balls, so it rolls instead of sliding and keeps the cutter square. Broach one Bearing Steel Stock in the Broach Press to cut its two ball tracks (Guide Rail Blank), then harden the blank in the Quench Vat with 250 mB water (160 ticks, 12 FE/t). Craft the guide with a Tempered Steel carriage on top, two Bearing Balls either side of the Hardened Guide Rail, and a Pressure Gasket below as the end seal wiper. An unhardened blank, an iron block or a sintered bushing (a sliding guide) does not fit. Bearing Steel comes from the Kiln and the balls from the Pressure Press, both before this tier. The vat is hopper- and pipe-fed, so rails can be hardened automatically; broaching is hand-fed.

The Spindle Gearbox steps the motion down so the mill head turns slowly with high torque. Gears are made in two steps, like real powder-metal gears: the Pressure Press compacts 3 Bronze Powder Blend into a fragile Green Gear Compact (100 ticks, 6 FE/t), then the Copper Hot Press sinters that compact into a Sintered Bronze Gear (160 ticks, 10 FE/t). Pressed-and-sintered bronze suits slow, lightly loaded gearing like this; hardened steel gears come later. Broach one Tool Steel Stock in the Broach Press for two rectangular Shaft Keys; one locks the hub to the Drive Shaft so torque reaches the cutter instead of the gear slipping. A round Broached Pin cannot transfer torque across this keyed hub. Put one key at the gearbox bottom-left, two gears either side of a Sealed Steel Plate housing on top, a Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing either side of the Drive Shaft, and one Lubricating Oil in the bottom centre. Press 8 forge:seeds in the Pressure Press for 160 ticks at 10 FE/t per oil. The oil bath splashes over the gears; Bearing Grease cannot replace it. Each journal bearing uses two Sintered Bronze Bushings, two forge:ingots/copper and one pressed Lubricating Oil in a crafting grid. Feed 3 Bronze Powder Blend into the Copper Hot Press for each bushing (120 ticks, 10 FE/t); its porous bronze sleeve holds oil at the rotating shaft while the copper end collars retain it. A loose dry bushing cannot replace the assembled bearing. Oil-film pressure, supply plumbing and wear are abstracted, so this is not a simulated fluid bearing. Hopper blend and seeds into their presses, extract outputs below, and automate the final grid crafts with ordinary crafting equipment. A bare plate or loose Drive Shaft cannot replace the gearbox.

Right-click the controller with feedstock from a loaded milling recipe. One complete batch of that recipe's input count loads into the controller; after 40 ticks, right-click with an empty hand to collect the output. A busy controller refuses another batch without consuming it. Missing or outward-facing pistons, anvil or redstone stop operation. One Tool Steel Stock mills into two Governor Flyweights, the balanced bobs of the Corona Collector's Flyweight Governor. Recovery never exceeds the craft cost: one mud bricks block returns one packed mud, and one purpur block returns one popped chorus fruit.

It runs 22 exclusive datapack milling recipes. Four glass panes give optic powder for the Heliostat Etcher; batches of andesite, diorite and granite yield gravel, while calcite yields sand. Sandstone and smooth sandstone recover sand; their red variants recover red sand. Quartz, purpur, bone, amethyst, brick, mud brick and nether brick blocks recover their component materials. Prismarine variants recover shards (prismarine and prismarine bricks each return four), and dripstone blocks recover pointed dripstone. These are separate inputs with distinct recovery paths rather than duplicate color recipes. JEI's Milling category lists loaded input counts and outputs; click the Milling Gantry catalyst to browse them. The gantry accepts hand-fed stock: hold the listed input count and right-click a formed controller to load one timed batch. For automation, insert valid milling stock into the controller from any face except the bottom and extract products from the bottom; reach these covered faces through Stock Hatches. Each formed batch takes 40 ticks; breaking the structure pauses processing without consuming stock. The controller buffers one input stack and one output stack, saves both and its face modes, and exposes Forge item handlers to hoppers or pipes. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to cycle the clicked face through input, output and disabled; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered output. It has no FE port.

The Power Contactor needs one Stamped Contactor Enclosure in its bottom-left craft slot. Make it from two Sealed Steel Plates in the Pressure Press for 140 ticks at 10 FE/t; three remaining plates brace the corners. The stamped box protects the busbar, wound coils and Limit Switch from exposed debris. Loose plates cannot replace the enclosure. Transfer the press output into the contactor grid, then use that contactor at the Milling Gantry top centre. Contact separation and ingress protection are represented by the part rather than simulated.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
